questions.question: You accidentally drop a colleague's coffee cup on their laptop. What is the most appropriate immediate response?
options: It's okay, don't worry about it.
I'm so sorry. I didn't mean to do that.
That's fine, I have another one.
You should have been more careful.
questions.answer: I'm so sorry. I didn't mean to do that.

questions.question: A friend asks for your advice on choosing a university course. How should you respond?
options: I think you should just pick the easiest one.
I'm not sure, but I think you should consider your interests.
That's a bad idea, you'll fail.
Go to the library and read about it yourself.
questions.answer: I'm not sure, but I think you should consider your interests.

questions.question: Someone offers you a ride home after work. Which response is the most polite and natural?
options: No thanks, I prefer to walk.
That's very kind of you, but I'll take the bus.
Sure, thanks. I'll get in.
I don't need a ride, you're driving.
questions.answer: That's very kind of you, but I'll take the bus.

questions.question: During a meeting, a colleague disagrees with your proposal. What is the best way to respond?
options: You're wrong, my idea is the only correct one.
I see your point, but I believe we should also consider the budget.
That's ridiculous, nobody will like it.
Fine, I'll change my mind now.
questions.answer: I see your point, but I believe we should also consider the budget.

questions.question: You need to ask a teacher for clarification on an assignment. Which phrasing is most appropriate?
options: I don't understand this question.
Can you explain this part of the assignment again, please?
Why did you write that? It's confusing.
I think the answer is wrong.
questions.answer: Can you explain this part of the assignment again, please?
